components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main action button. Inquisitive Violet background, near-white text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; white-space: nowrap; font-family: Charter, 'Bitstream Charter', 'Sitka Text', Cambria, serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; background: oklch(43.2% 0.232 292.759); color: oklch(0.985 0 0); border: none; border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 16px; height: 36px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(43.2% 0.232 292.759 / 0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid oklch(0.708 0 0 / 0.5); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard text input with border stroke and focus ring.
components.css: .ds-input { font-family: Charter, 'Bitstream Charter', 'Sitka Text', Cambria, serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.5; background: transparent; color: oklch(0.145 0 0); border: 1px solid oklch(0.922 0 0); border-radius: 8px; padding: 4px 12px; height: 36px; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: oklch(0.556 0 0); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: oklch(0.708 0 0); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px oklch(0.708 0 0 / 0.5); outline: none; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Content container with subtle border and minimal shadow.
components.html:
Why do we ask?
A question about questions
Because curiosity is the point.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 24px; background: oklch(1 0 0); color: oklch(0.145 0 0); border: 1px solid oklch(0.922 0 0); border-radius: 14px; padding: 24px 0; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); font-family: Charter, 'Bitstream Charter', 'Sitka Text', Cambria, serif; } .ds-card-header { display: grid; gap: 8px; padding: 0 24px; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.3; } .ds-card-desc { font-size: 1rem; color: oklch(0.556 0 0); } .ds-card-content { padding: 0 24px; font-size: 1.25rem; line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Navigation Bar
components.description: Floating violet desktop navigation bar. The primary brand moment.
components.html: QuestionsInterviewsTopics
components.css: .ds-navbar { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; background: oklch(43.2% 0.232 292.759); border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 12px; gap: 12px; box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 4px 6px -4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); font-family: Charter, 'Bitstream Charter', 'Sitka Text', Cambria, serif; } .ds-nav-link { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: oklch(0.985 0 0); text-decoration: none; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-nav-link:hover { background: oklch(0 0 0 / 0.2); } .ds-nav-link--active { background: oklch(0 0 0 / 0.15); } .ds-nav-actions { display: flex; gap: 4px; margin-left: auto; }

narrative.overview:
A warm, inviting room where questions are the main event. The design carries the typographic confidence of a well-edited column, where every question sits with presence and every answer reads with clarity. This is not a feed to scroll past; it is a space to linger in.

The system rejects corporate density (no Stack Overflow utility grids), generic social media sameness (no infinite scroll without character), and sterile SaaS polish (no dashboards pretending to be clever). It also rejects the disposable chaos of old anonymous Q&A platforms. Every surface should feel like it was set by someone who cares about the conversation, not someone who cares about engagement metrics.
keyCharacteristics: Serif-first typography that reads like editorial, not software
A single violet accent used with restraint, giving questions visual weight
Generous whitespace that lets questions breathe
Flat surfaces with minimal elevation; depth comes from typography and color, not shadows
Playful confidence: warm enough to invite participation, sharp enough to be taken seriously

rules.name: The Parlor Rule
rules.body: Inquisitive Violet appears on no more than 15% of any given screen. Its rarity makes it meaningful.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: No pure #000 or #fff in production. Every neutral is tinted warm by the serif typography's natural character.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Charter is the only typeface. No sans-serif for UI chrome, no monospace for code blocks (unless displaying actual code).

rules.name: The Generous Base Rule
rules.body: Body text is 20px, not 16px. Reducing it to match standard app sizing destroys the editorial feel.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only on the navigation bar and dropdown menus.

dos: Do use Charter at 20px base size for all body text.
Do let questions breathe with generous vertical spacing (24px+ between question items).
Do keep the violet accent under 15% surface coverage per screen.
Do use tonal layering (Whisper Gray on Warm Paper) instead of shadows for visual hierarchy.
Do use the floating violet navigation bar as the primary brand moment on desktop.
Do test color contrast against WCAG AA for both light and dark themes.
donts: Don't use corporate Q&A density (Stack Overflow's cramped utility grid).
Don't create generic social media feed patterns.
Don't apply sterile SaaS dashboard aesthetics.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as colored accent stripes.
Don't apply gradient text via background-clip.
Don't reduce the base font size below 20px.
Don't use em dashes in UI copy.
Don't add shadows to cards or content areas.
